# Receipt OCR: Comprehensive Project Research Report

**Evidence snapshot:** `D:/other/ocrr`, inspected on 2026-10-30. Paths are relative to this root. Notebook cell indices are zero-based. This is an evidence audit, not a new experimental run.

**Reading and evidence policy.** All first-party source, documentation, configuration, the ground-truth table, five notebooks and every saved output were read. All six embedded notebook PNGs and the distinct receipt images were visually inspected. Python and JavaScript lockfiles were parsed; the built frontend application was checked against source. All installed dependency files and caches are inventoried in Appendix A, but third-party implementation source and binary caches are not treated as authored research. No inference, training, installation, server, test, or notebook was executed during this audit. Only this report was created. Saved metrics retain their original exact display strings; underlying precision absent from the files is **NOT FOUND IN PROJECT**. Interpretations and proposed improvements are labeled. No external research or web claims have been added.

The appendices preserve complete first-party textual files, complete notebook cell/output transcripts, all notebook figures, reference annotations, dependency versions, and the full file inventory. Thus an AI without the project can inspect the exact methods and evidence. Images use embedded data URIs; descriptions remain readable if a Markdown renderer does not support them.

## 1. Project Overview

### 1.1 Objective and problem

**Receipt OCR** converts receipt images into vendor, date, grand total, and line-item name/price records. It combines OpenCV preprocessing, pretrained PaddleOCR, deterministic extraction or local Llama 3.2 extraction through Ollama, a FastAPI backend, and React UI. The stated objective is a fully local, open-source receipt OCR application. Python package metadata names it `receipt-ocr`, version `0.1.0`; API metadata uses version `1.0.0`. (sources: `README.md`; `pyproject.toml`; `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`; `api/main.py`)

The practical problem is reconstructing structured records from OCR fragments containing names, barcode-like numbers, prices, tax flags, coupon lines, payment records, and footer text. Saved prototypes demonstrate misidentifying stray rightmost digits as prices and losing name/price associations when individual OCR tokens are serialized one per line. (sources: `notebooks/02_ocr.ipynb`, cells 14 and 19; `notebooks/03_extraction.ipynb`, cells 13–14; `notebooks/04_llm_extraction.ipynb`, cells 6 and 12)

### 1.2 Output and defensible contribution

The runtime API returns:

```json
{
  "vendor": "string",
  "date": "string or null",
  "total": 0.0,
  "items": [{"item_name": "string", "price": 0.0}]
}
```

`date` is an optional string, not a validated ISO date. Values are floats; the API has no currency or quantity field. The LLM requests `name` internally, mapped to `item_name` by the API. (sources: `api/main.py`, `ReceiptData`, `Item`, `analyze_llm`; `src/extractor_llm.py`)

The evidence supports an **engineering case study**: local integration, interchangeable extraction paths, spatial text reconstruction, a subtotal/total-anchored price-repair heuristic, and a small transparent prototype comparison. A new trained model, state-of-the-art claim, formal novelty analysis, or proven generalizable contribution is **NOT FOUND IN PROJECT**. (sources: `src/`; `api/main.py`; `web/src/App.jsx`; notebooks 01–05)

Documentation marks the development phases complete. That is an author checklist status, not independent validation. The only quantitative saved evaluation concerns older notebook prototypes on one receipt; current source differs materially. (sources: `docs/TASKS_TRACKER.md`; `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`; `notebooks/05_benchmark.ipynb`; `src/`)

## 2. Background & Motivation

### 2.1 Recorded rationale

The notebooks motivate grayscale as channel reduction, adaptive thresholding for uneven lighting, upscaling for small text, and deskewing for horizontal recognition. Rules are described as deterministic, fast, and debuggable; local LLMs are motivated by brittle regexes and contextual interpretation of noisy structure. Local processing is an explicit design goal. These are project rationales, not controlled findings. (sources: `notebooks/01_preprocessing.ipynb`, markdown cells; `notebooks/03_extraction.ipynb`, cells 0 and 14; `notebooks/04_llm_extraction.ipynb`, cells 0 and 15; `README.md`)

`docs/LEARNING_NOTES.md` asserts that preprocessing significantly improves accuracy and can matter more than model tuning. No measured preprocessing ablation or OCR accuracy comparison supports this in the supplied files. Its claim that Llama 3.2 (3B) runs well on consumer hardware lacks a hardware/resource record. (source: `docs/LEARNING_NOTES.md`)

## 4. Methodology

### 4.1 Current application pipeline

1. **Image selection:** React accepts browser MIME types beginning `image/`, from drag/drop or picker, and creates a preview object URL. Default mode is `rules`. (source: `web/src/App.jsx`, state and file/drag handlers)
2. **Upload:** Single-mode analysis posts multipart data to `/analyze/rules` or `/analyze/llm` at hard-coded `http://localhost:8000`. Compare mode uses two separate forms and `Promise.all`; both endpoints independently preprocess/OCR the same image. (source: `web/src/App.jsx`, `analyzeImage`)
3. **Temporary storage:** FastAPI saves `temp/<uuid><original suffix>`, falling back to `.jpg` when filename is absent. It closes the upload stream. (source: `api/main.py`, `save_upload_file`)
4. **Preprocessing:** Decode image, grayscale, CLAHE, blur, Otsu threshold, closing, cubic scaling, deskew. Decode failure raises `ValueError`. Preprocessed arrays remain in memory. (sources: `src/image_processor.py`; API endpoints)
5. **Lazy OCR:** A global engine starts as `None`, initialized on first analysis and reused. Health does not initialize or verify it. (source: `api/main.py`, `get_ocr_engine`, `health_check`)
6. **Recognition:** Convert grayscale arrays to BGR, call PaddleOCR, parse first page into text/confidence/boxes/centers, discard empty text, sort by `(center_y, center_x)`. (source: `src/ocr_engine.py`)
7. **Extraction:** Rules select metadata and spatial item rows, then repair candidate prices. LLM mode reconstructs rows and calls Ollama with system/user prompts, then parses JSON. (sources: extractors; OCR `get_full_text`)
8. **Normalization:** LLM items map `name` or `item_name` to API fields; missing names/vendor become `Unknown`, invalid or missing numeric prices/total become `0.0`, date remains supplied text. Pydantic models enforce outer response types. Analysis exceptions become HTTP `500` with exception text. (source: `api/main.py`)
9. **Cleanup/display:** API attempts upload deletion in `finally`, suppressing cleanup errors. Single-result UI shows header fields and full items; compare shows header fields and item counts, plus combined wall time. UI uses dollar signs and `toFixed(2)` regardless of inferred currency. (sources: `api/main.py`; `web/src/App.jsx`)

### 4.2 Historical pipeline underlying saved results

Notebook 01 demonstrates preprocessing and saves a PNG. Notebook 02 **selects the original image**, calls `predict`, parses polygon boxes, keeps empty tokens, sorts only by Y, and saves OCR JSON. Notebook 03 reads JSON and exports older rules outputs. Notebook 04 serializes tokens one per newline, calls an older generic prompt with no explicit decoding options, and exports LLM items. Notebook 05 scores those CSVs against 26 annotations. Therefore the saved benchmark does not evaluate notebook 01 preprocessing or current API modules. (sources: executable cells in notebooks 01–05)

### 5.2 Image operations and equations

These equations formalize operations selected in source; they are not quoted mathematical derivations from project documentation.

- Prototype adaptive threshold: `B(x,y)=255` when `G(x,y)>GaussianWeightedMean_11x11(x,y)-2`, otherwise `0`. (source: notebook 01 cell 9)
- Current Otsu threshold: threshold blurred grayscale using OpenCV's global Otsu-selected value; pixels above threshold map to `255`, otherwise `0`. Otsu derivation is **NOT FOUND IN PROJECT**. (source: `preprocess_receipt`)
- Dimensions: `W'=int(W*s)`, `H'=int(H*s)` with cubic interpolation. Default `s=1.5`; lighter function `s=2.0`. (source: `src/image_processor.py`)
- Segment angle: `theta_i=degrees(atan2(y2_i-y1_i,x2_i-x1_i))`; keep `abs(theta_i)<45`; estimate `theta=median(theta_i)`. No valid lines or `abs(theta)<0.5` returns unchanged. Otherwise rotate around `(W//2,H//2)`, scale `1.0`, fixed original canvas, cubic interpolation, replicated border. (source: `deskew`)

| Operation | Exact current parameters |
|---|---|
| CLAHE | `clipLimit=2.0`, `tileGridSize=(8,8)` |
| Gaussian blur | kernel `(3,3)`, sigma `0` |
| Global threshold | threshold `0`, maximum `255`, `THRESH_BINARY + THRESH_OTSU` |
| Closing | `MORPH_RECT`, kernel size `(2,1)`, `MORPH_CLOSE` |
| Canny | `50`, `150`, `apertureSize=3` |
| HoughLinesP | rho `1`, theta `pi/180`, threshold `100`, `minLineLength=100`, `maxLineGap=10` |
| Rotation | `INTER_CUBIC`, `BORDER_REPLICATE` |

(source: `src/image_processor.py`)

The closing comment says “vertical,” but the supplied size `(2,1)` is width/height, inconsistent with that wording. Signature default is `1.5`, while an argument description and later comment mention `2.0`/`2×`. The executable values above take precedence. (source: same file)

### 5.3 OCR geometry and row reconstruction

For box `(x1,y1,x2,y2)`, `cy=(y1+y2)/2`, `cx=(x1+x2)/2`. Current parser rounds confidence to `3` decimals, boxes to integers, centers to `1` decimal; then sorts Y/X. Thus saved values may already have project-applied rounding; this report adds none. v3 parsing uses `rec_texts`, `rec_scores`, `rec_boxes`; legacy parsing derives bounds from polygons. Only first page is handled. (source: `src/ocr_engine.py`, `_parse_results`)

Let `h=median(abs(y2-y1))` over positive-height boxes, fallback `20.0`; row tolerance `tau=0.55*h`. Traverse sorted tokens and join current token to previous token's row if `abs(cy_current-cy_previous)<=tau`, else start a row. Sort each row by left X. LLM text joins row tokens with two spaces and rows with newline. Adjacent-token chaining can create rows with overall span greater than `tau`; horizontal distances are not encoded numerically. (sources: OCR `_compute_line_height`, `_group_into_rows`, `get_full_text`; rules `extract_items`)

### 5.4 Current deterministic rules

**Vendor:** first acceptable text among top `5` tokens, minimum length `2`, excluding substrings `receipt`, `welcome`, `tax invoice`, `copy`, `payment`. Fallback `Unknown Vendor`. Confidence and font size are unused, despite notebook motivation. (source: `extract_vendor`)

**Date:** scan individual text and adjacent-token pair concatenations. Patterns cover ISO, slash dates with two/four-digit years, dashed numeric dates, abbreviated month forms. Use `dayfirst=False`; two-digit-year result above `2030` is reduced by `100`. Return first valid `%Y-%m-%d`, else `None`. (source: `extract_date`)

**Total:** take maximum decimal amount within individual tokens containing word-boundary `total`, excluding `subtotal` and `sub total`; else maximum within `tend` tokens; else maximum decimal amount in the bottom half of tokens; fallback `0.0`. Unlike prototype, keyword passes do not inspect next token. **Subtotal:** first decimal amount within token containing `subtotal`, `sub total`, or `sub-total`, else `0.0`. (sources: `extract_total`, `extract_subtotal`)

**Items:** use adaptive grouping, skip any row containing a keyword substring, remove standalone barcode-like tokens (six or more digits with up to three letters), remove supported trailing flags, require at least two remaining tokens, parse final token as unsigned price, assemble prior tokens as name, strip final flags, reject empty names and summary names and price `>9999`, then correct prices. Same-token name plus price is unsupported by this design. (source: `extract_items`)

Skip set includes `coupon`, payment/summary metadata, and short substring `aid`; filters can remove legitimate names. The unsigned amount regex rejects negative prices. Exact regexes/keyword sets are preserved in Appendix E. (source: `src/extractor_rules.py`)

### 5.5 Price-correction heuristic

Choose anchor `A=subtotal` if positive, else `total`; return unchanged when `A<=0`. Candidate prices satisfy `8.0<=p_i<9.0`; cap to first `15`. With `S=sum(p_i)`, search masks:

`m* = argmin_m abs(S - 8.0*popcount(m) - A)`, for `m=0,...,2^n-1`.

Start from mask zero; update only on strict improvement, retaining earliest ties. Selected prices become `round(p_i-8.0,2)`. Group candidates by identical original price; for group size `>=3`, if `num_corrected>=len(group)//2`, correct remaining members too. This is implemented behavior, not a strict majority: for size `3`, one correction triggers propagation. (source: `src/extractor_rules.py`, `_correct_prices`)

Search has at most `2^15=32768` masks including zero and loops over candidates per mask, `O(n*2^n)` for capped `n`. Every repair subtracts the same `8.0`; objective chooses correction count, not which same-count subset is right. Missing lines/coupons, tax, and legitimate `8.XX` prices can mislead it; propagation may worsen original objective. Validation or saved ablation is **NOT FOUND IN PROJECT**. (source: function; static interpretation)

### 5.6 LLM prompting and parsing

Current prompt specializes in US grocery/retail receipts, requests JSON only, explains `8–14` digit codes and `1–2` letter flags, negative coupons, `TOTAL` versus `SUBTOTAL`, ISO dates and null unknowns. It includes Walmart date `07/28/17`, total `98.21`, `PET TOY` `1.97`, coupon `-1.00`. Call options are `temperature=0.0`, `num_predict=2048`; model default `llama3.2`. The complete prompt is reproduced in Appendix E. (source: `src/extractor_llm.py`)

The current worked example overlaps the sole reference receipt, creating contamination risk if evaluating this updated prompt on the same sample. Historical notebook prompt is generic without this example, so the risk must not be attributed retrospectively to saved prototype metrics. (sources: current prompt; notebook 04 cell 8; reference CSV/image)

Parser strips fences, attempts direct `json.loads`, then greedy `r'\{.*\}'` with DOTALL and parses again. Failure prints first `500` response characters and returns `{}`; extraction exceptions also return `{}`. Schema-constrained decoding, retries, validated field semantics, explicit seed and determinism evidence are **NOT FOUND IN PROJECT**. Temperature zero alone is not demonstrated hallucination prevention or reproducibility. (source: `ReceiptLLM`)

### 5.7 Core pseudocode

```text
ANALYZE(upload, mode):
    path <- save UUID-named upload
    try:
        image <- current preprocessing(path)
        tokens <- lazy shared OCR.process(image)
        if mode == rules:
            vendor, date, total, subtotal <- metadata heuristics(tokens)
            rows <- adjacent-Y grouping with 0.55*median-height tolerance
            items <- skip summaries, remove codes/flags, parse last prices
            items <- capped anchor-based 8.XX -> 0.XX correction
            return vendor, date, total, items
        text <- X-sorted visual rows joined by two spaces/newlines
        raw <- Ollama(system prompt, text, temperature=0.0, num_predict=2048)
        data <- fence stripping + JSON parse + brace-search fallback
        return API field/type normalization(data)
    finally:
        attempt upload deletion
```

(sources: `api/main.py`; four core modules)

### 7.2 Exact scoring definition

`sim(a,b)`: convert both values to lowercase strings; empty gives `0.0`; either-direction substring gives `1.0`; otherwise `SequenceMatcher(None,a,b).ratio()`. (source: notebook 05 cell 8)

For each extracted item in order, inspect unused ground-truth rows and maximize:

`score(i,j)=sim(name_i,name_j)+0.5*I(abs(price_i-price_j)<0.01)`.

Strict `>` updates preserve first ties. Accept best candidate if `sim>=0.6` or `(price_equal and sim>0.3)`; mark reference used. Accepted records are `TP` even when price is wrong. Unmatched predictions are `FP`, unmatched references `FN`. This greedy matching is order dependent and does not retry another candidate after best-candidate rejection. (source: notebook 05 cell 8)

`precision=TP/predicted_count`

`recall=TP/reference_count`

`F1=2*precision*recall/(precision+recall)`

`name_percent=100*mean(similarity over TP)`

`aligned_price_percent=100*mean(I(abs(pred_price-reference_price)<0.01) over TP)`

`bag_price_percent=100*sum_v min(count_pred(round(price,2)=v),count_ref(round(price,2)=v))/reference_price_count`.

Zero denominator returns zero. Bag metric drops missing prices and ignores name/alignment; it is reference-price coverage, with no direct penalty for extra incorrect predicted prices. Summary prints recall to one percent decimal, F1 to three decimals, other percentages to one decimal. Precision is calculated but not printed; no exact saved decimal precision value exists. (source: notebook 05 cell 10)

Metrics concern extracted names, prices and item retrieval, but formal threshold justification/tuning set is **NOT FOUND IN PROJECT**. CER/WER, quantity accuracy, vendor/date/total accuracy, calibration, full-receipt exact match and stage-wise OCR attribution are not evaluated. The introductory `>85%`/Levenshtein text does not describe executable scoring. (source: notebook 05)

## 9. Analysis & Interpretation

### 9.1 Comparative findings and scope

Historical LLM has higher saved recall, F1, matched-name similarity, aligned-price accuracy, and independent price coverage under this evaluator. This supports a within-receipt comparison only; statistical significance, current-API gains, multi-vendor superiority, or robust generalization are not demonstrated. (source: notebook 05 cell 10)

Visible outputs support a plausible mechanism: rules keep barcodes/flags and misread final noise as prices; LLM removes many codes and preserves more price values. LLM also splits names, shifts prices, omits products/coupon, aggregates duplicates and violates date format. These are observed trade-offs rather than proof of reliable semantic understanding. (sources: notebook 03 cell 13; notebook 04 cell 12; notebook 05 cell 11)

### 9.2 Metric interpretation

Substring override scores `PET` versus `PET TOY`, `FLOPPY` versus `FLOPPY PUPPY`, and `SUNFLWR` versus `STKO SUNFLWR` as `1.0`. Therefore `100.0%` denotes conditional mean relaxed similarity among accepted matches, not exact names or full-reference coverage. TP accepts wrong prices, so F1 is relaxed item retrieval, not joint name/price correctness. Bag-price coverage says nothing about which item owns each price. (sources: notebook 05 cells 8, 10; reference CSV; LLM output)

### 9.3 Error analysis

| Failure | Evidence | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Rightmost noise becomes price | Rules toy `7.0`, carrots `1.0`, collards `7.0` | Last-token assumption is brittle. |
| Summary rows become items | `VISA TEND` `98.21`, `CHANGE DUE` `0.0` | Prototype summary filtering insufficient. |
| Subtotal confusion | Rules total `93.62`, actual grand total `98.21` | `total` substring matches `SUBTOTAL`. |
| Missed date | Rules `None`; OCR has `07/28/17` | Prototype lacks two-digit-year slash pattern. |
| Price shifts | Four recorded LLM price errors | Token-per-line structure loses associations; causal role not ablated. |
| Repeated instance loss | Four sunflower reference rows; one LLM `SUNFLWR` qty `4` | Aggregation conflicts with per-instance scoring. |
| Coupon loss | Reference `-1.00`; absent in both lists | Neither prototype captures coupon correctly. |
| Date format violation | LLM `07/28/17` | Parseable JSON does not enforce semantic schema. |

Sources: notebooks 02–05; CSV/image.

Notebook 05 prose attributes recall mainly to upstream OCR, but saved OCR includes `DOG TREAT`, both `PED PCH 1` entries, coupon text, and four sunflower entries that extraction loses/reorganizes. OCR-only bottleneck is therefore an unproven hypothesis; stage-wise labeling is needed. Its conclusion also calls gains significant, names perfect, and improvement “+27%”; there is no significance test and the exact displayed price metrics are `73.1%` versus `46.2%`. Do not reuse prose as a validated causal or relative-gain claim. (sources: notebook 02 cells 14/19; notebook 04 cell 12; notebook 05 cells 10/12)

## 10. Limitations & Issues

These are static audit findings unless explicitly tied to saved behavior; none is presented as a newly executed test result.

1. **Single receipt, no held-out validation.** No generalization estimate or statistical inference is justified. (sources: image/CSV; benchmark)
2. **Missing exports.** Historical success messages reference OCR JSON, PNG and CSVs; only notebook outputs survive in supplied `out/` snapshot. (sources: notebooks; inventory)
3. **Prototype/current drift.** Preprocessing, OCR options/method/geometry, grouping, rules, prompt and decoding changed. Current performance is unknown. (sources: notebooks versus `src/`)
4. **Relaxed scoring.** Substring names, wrong-price TP, greedy order dependence and unaligned bag values can overstate strict correctness. (source: notebook 05)
5. **Prompt overlap.** Current prompt uses identity/date/total/examples from sole receipt, threatening evaluation of updated prompt on this sample. Historical prompt differs. (sources: prompts; CSV/image)
6. **Current total/subtotal token issue.** Keyword extraction requires amount within same OCR token; separate amount tokens bypass it. Total exclusion does not handle `sub-total` though subtotal does. Fallback may choose an unrelated bottom-half maximum. (source: rules)
7. **Date inconsistency.** Current month-first parsing contradicts fixture expectation; fixed `2030` cutoff can misinterpret future dates; API does not validate format. (sources: rules/test/API)
8. **Coupon mismatch.** Rules explicitly skip coupon and reject negative prices; annotations include one; LLM prompt requests negatives. (sources: extractors/CSV)
9. **Unvalidated correction.** Fixed `8.0` changes cannot distinguish same-count subsets; repeated-price threshold is not majority; genuine prices may be altered and propagation can worsen anchor error. (source: `_correct_prices`)
10. **Grouping/filter edge cases.** Adjacent-Y chaining can merge rows; short substring filters may reject names; same-token items/wrapped names/quantity-price columns lack robust handling. (sources: rules/OCR)
11. **Comment drift.** Actual scaling `1.5` versus `2×` prose, and kernel orientation wording mismatch. (source: image processor)
12. **LLM error concealment.** Ollama failure can return `{}` and API emits `Unknown`, zero total, empty items as apparent success. Parser accepts JSON without dict/item-schema verification; `items=null` or scalar entries can trigger errors. Numeric invalids become zero, conflating unknown and real zero. (sources: LLM/API)
13. **Blocking async work.** Synchronous OCR/OpenCV/Ollama/filesystem calls execute directly in async handlers. Browser parallel requests do not prove parallel computation; global engine has no synchronization/concurrency test. (sources: API/UI)
14. **Service/input gaps.** Health is constant; no OCR/Ollama readiness checks, authentication, upload-size/dimension limit, server MIME validation or explicit request timeouts. CORS permits all origins/methods/headers and credentials. (source: API)
15. **Upload cleanup edges.** Save occurs before handler try/finally; failed partial copy lacks endpoint cleanup coverage. Cleanup exceptions are suppressed; temp files lack provenance. (source: API/temp)
16. **UI state.** Object URLs never revoked; modes can change during processing; result labels use current rather than submitted mode; response-time state is not reset on new file; compare lacks item tables and one failure rejects both-result display. (source: UI)
17. **Offline qualification.** Local inference does not establish fully offline deployment: packages/models download, CSS imports Google Fonts. (sources: README, setup notebooks, App.css)
18. **Environment ambiguity.** README Node minimum conflicts with locked engines; historical versions/hardware absent. Both OpenCV and contrib packages resolve and may share `cv2`; actual compatibility unverified. (sources: lockfiles/README)
19. **Weak test evidence.** API script prints/catches without asserting; LLM test mocked; tiny fixture tests at import; no saved run logs or broad receipt regressions. (sources: tests)
20. **License missing.** README advertises MIT and links root `LICENSE`, which is absent. Dataset/model license documentation is also **NOT FOUND IN PROJECT**. (sources: README/tree)

| Strict joint name/price metrics and optimal assignment | Relaxed/greedy score caveats | Exact names, aligned prices, instance F1, receipt exact match |
| OCR reference text/geometry and stage diagnostics | OCR-only bottleneck unproven | CER/WER, coordinate alignment, grouping/extraction attribution |
| Ablate preprocessing, row text, examples, correction | No causal evaluation | One component changed at a time |
| Evidence-sensitive price repair | Underdetermined fixed subtraction | Genuine `8.XX`, missing lines, coupon/tax regressions |
| Schema validation and explicit missing/error states | Parse/type failures and zero defaults | Malformed JSON/outage/invalid type tests |
| Standardize quantities/coupons/dates/taxes | Divergent schemas/fixtures | Annotated field semantics |
| Bound inputs and schedule blocking work | Current synchronous pipeline | Concurrency, cold/warm latency/resource profiles |
| OCR once for compare mode | Duplicate processing | Shared-input comparison and stage times |
| Bundle fonts/models for offline deployment | External assets/downloads | Offline end-to-end check |

Sources for rationale: files cited in §§3–11. No gain or expected performance number is claimed.

## 13. Suggested Paper Structure

| Paper section | Report material | Caution |
|---|---|---|
| Abstract | §§1, 4, 8, 10 | Single-receipt prototype scope; exact saved metrics |
| Introduction | §§1–2 | No unsupported prevalence/cost/novelty claims |
| Related Work | §2 | Formal bibliography absent; independently verify literature |
| Method | §§4–6 | Explicitly choose historical or current pipeline |
| Experiments | §§3, 7 | 26 rows, one receipt, relaxed evaluator, missing metadata |
| Results | §8 | Documentation timings are not measured runs |
| Discussion | §§9–10 | Metric inflation, structural errors, duplicates/coupons, drift |
| Conclusion | §§1, 9–10, 12 | Engineering feasibility and limited comparison only |
| Supplement | §14 | Complete source, annotations, outputs, figures, versions |

### Candidate key contributions

1. Local image-to-structured-receipt application integrating OpenCV/PaddleOCR/Ollama/FastAPI/React. (sources: core/API/UI)
2. Two extraction approaches behind consistent API fields. (sources: extractors/API)
3. Median-height spatial row reconstruction for LLM input. (source: OCR module)
4. Capped subtotal/total-anchored price repair, explicitly unvalidated. (source: rules)
5. Transparent one-receipt prototype comparison with full predictions and saved metrics. (sources: notebooks 03–05)
6. Failure analysis of code/flag contamination, shifted prices, duplicate aggregation, subtotal confusion and coupons. (sources: notebooks/CSV/image)
7. Evidence separation between notebook prototypes, current code, examples and assertions. This point describes the present audit, not an original learned algorithm. (sources: cross-file audit)

These are suggested framing points, **not verified novel research contributions**. Literature priority and publication-level empirical validation are **NOT FOUND IN PROJECT**.

### B. Glossary

| Term | Meaning in this project |
|---|---|
| OCR | Optical character recognition, returning text, geometry and confidence. |
| LLM | Large language model parsing OCR text into structured records. |
| POC | Proof of concept, notebook prototype stage. |
| API / REST | HTTP interface implemented with FastAPI. |
| JSON | Object serialization used for OCR and LLM results. |
| CSV | Comma-separated reference and prediction tables. |
| CLAHE | Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization. |
| BGR / RGB | OpenCV versus display color channel order. |
| UPC | Product barcode-like code stripped by extraction. |
| bbox | Rectangle `[x1,y1,x2,y2]`. |
| GT | Ground truth reference annotation. |
| TP / FP / FN | Accepted prediction / unmatched prediction / unmatched reference under relaxed evaluator. |
| F1 | Harmonic mean of retrieval precision and recall. |
| Bag-of-prices | Multiset price intersection divided by reference price count. |
| CORS | Cross-Origin Resource Sharing policy. |
| HMR | Hot Module Replacement in Vite development. |
| MKL-DNN / oneDNN | Acceleration option disabled in current OCR. |
| CER / WER | Character/word error rate, proposed future metrics, not measured here. |
| UUID | Upload filename identifier. |
| ISO date | Requested `YYYY-MM-DD`, not enforced by API type. |
| null / None | JSON/Python missing-value representations. |

Sources: terminology and identifiers in source/notebooks/docs; CER/WER are explicitly proposals.

````py
from fastapi import FastAPI, UploadFile, File, HTTPException
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import Dict, Any, List, Optional
import shutil
import os
from pathlib import Path
import uuid

# Import core modules
from src.image_processor import preprocess_receipt
from src.ocr_engine import ReceiptOCR
from src.extractor_rules import extract_receipt_data, _correct_prices, extract_subtotal
from src.extractor_llm import ReceiptLLM

app = FastAPI(
    title="Receipt OCR API",
    description="Backend API for processing receipt images using PaddleOCR and LLMs",
    version="1.0.0"
)

# Configure CORS
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

# Initialize lightweight engines; PaddleOCR is loaded on the first analysis request.
ocr_engine = None
llm_engine = ReceiptLLM()

def get_ocr_engine() -> ReceiptOCR:
    global ocr_engine
    if ocr_engine is None:
        ocr_engine = ReceiptOCR()
    return ocr_engine

def as_float(value: Any, default: float = 0.0) -> float:
    try:
        return float(value) if value is not None else default
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default

# Temp directory for uploads
TEMP_DIR = Path("temp")
TEMP_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

class HealthResponse(BaseModel):
    status: str
    version: str

class Item(BaseModel):
    item_name: str
    price: float

class ReceiptData(BaseModel):
    vendor: str
    date: Optional[str]
    total: float
    items: List[Item]

@app.get("/health", response_model=HealthResponse)
async def health_check():
    """Health check endpoint to verify API is running."""
    return {
        "status": "healthy",
        "version": "1.0.0"
    }

@app.get("/")
async def root():
    return {"message": "Receipt OCR API is running. Visit /docs for documentation."}

def save_upload_file(upload_file: UploadFile) -> Path:
    """Save upload file to temp directory."""
    try:
        file_ext = Path(upload_file.filename).suffix if upload_file.filename else ".jpg"
        file_name = f"{uuid.uuid4()}{file_ext}"
        file_path = TEMP_DIR / file_name
        
        with open(file_path, "wb") as buffer:
            shutil.copyfileobj(upload_file.file, buffer)
            
        return file_path
    finally:
        upload_file.file.close()

@app.post("/analyze/rules", response_model=ReceiptData)
async def analyze_rules(file: UploadFile = File(...)):
    """
    Analyze receipt using deterministic rules.
    Fast, valid for simple receipts.
    """
    temp_path = save_upload_file(file)
    try:
        # 1. Preprocess — returns numpy array in memory (no disk write needed)
        preprocessed_img = preprocess_receipt(temp_path)

        # 2. OCR — pass numpy array directly, skipping an extra disk round-trip
        ocr_results = get_ocr_engine().process(preprocessed_img)

        # 3. Extract using rules
        data = extract_receipt_data(ocr_results)

        return data

    except Exception as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e))
    finally:
        try:
            os.remove(temp_path)
        except:
            pass

@app.post("/analyze/llm", response_model=ReceiptData)
async def analyze_llm(file: UploadFile = File(...)):
    """
    Analyze receipt using Local LLM (Llama 3.2).
    Slower, but more robust for complex receipts.
    """
    temp_path = save_upload_file(file)
    try:
        # 1. Preprocess — numpy array in memory
        preprocessed_img = preprocess_receipt(temp_path)

        # 2. OCR — pass numpy array directly
        engine = get_ocr_engine()
        ocr_results = engine.process(preprocessed_img)

        # 3. Reconstruct columnar text for the LLM
        full_text = engine.get_full_text(ocr_results)

        # 4. LLM extraction
        data = llm_engine.extract(full_text)

        # 5. Normalise keys and types to match Pydantic model
        mapped_items = []
        for item in data.get("items", []):
            mapped_items.append({
                "item_name": item.get("name") or item.get("item_name") or "Unknown",
                "price": as_float(item.get("price"))
            })

        return {
            "vendor": data.get("vendor") or "Unknown",
            "date":   data.get("date"),
            "total":  as_float(data.get("total")),
            "items":  mapped_items,
        }

    except Exception as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e))
    finally:
        try:
            os.remove(temp_path)
        except:
            pass

````

````md
# 📚 Receipt OCR Learning Notes

> **Project:** Local Receipt OCR → Full-Stack Application  
> **Status:** ✅ Complete (All Phases)

---

## 🗺️ Project Phases

```
Phase 1: Setup    →  Phase 2: Notebooks  →  Phase 3: Modules  →  Phase 4: API  →  Phase 5: Frontend
   ✅                     ✅                     ✅                  ✅               ✅
```

---

## 📖 Key Learnings

### 1. Image Preprocessing Matters
- Grayscale + adaptive thresholding significantly improves OCR accuracy
- Deskewing rotated receipts prevents text line fragmentation
- Simple preprocessing often beats complex model tuning

### 2. PaddleOCR v3.x Changes
**Breaking Change:** Output format changed from tuples to `OCRResult` dict-like objects.

```python
# v2.x format (old)
line = [[bbox_points], (text, confidence)]

# v3.x format (new) - OCRResult object
result['rec_texts']   # List of texts
result['rec_scores']  # List of confidences  
result['rec_boxes']   # numpy array of boxes
```

### 3. Rules vs LLM Trade-offs

| Approach | Speed | Accuracy | Best For |
|----------|-------|----------|----------|
| Rules | ~35s | Good | Simple, structured receipts |
| LLM | ~75s | Better | Complex layouts, varied formats |

### 4. Local LLM Integration
- Ollama provides easy local LLM deployment
- Llama 3.2 (3B) runs well on consumer hardware
- Structured JSON prompts work well for extraction tasks

---

## 🏗️ Architecture Decisions

### Backend
- **FastAPI** for async performance
- **Single-file API** (`api/main.py`) for simplicity
- **Shared `src/` modules** between API and notebooks

### Frontend
- **Vite + React** for fast development
- **Vanilla CSS** with modern design (glassmorphism, dark theme)
- **Three modes**: Rules, LLM, Compare

---

## 📊 Output Schema

```json
{
  "vendor": "string",
  "date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "total": 0.00,
  "items": [
    {"item_name": "string", "price": 0.00}
  ]
}
```

---

## 🎯 Success Criteria (All Met ✅)

- [x] Full-stack application with UI
- [x] Two extraction modes (Rules + LLM)
- [x] Side-by-side comparison
- [x] 100% local processing
- [x] Well-documented codebase

#### Source: `README.md`

````md
# 📄 Receipt OCR

A **fully local, open-source** receipt OCR system that extracts structured data from receipt images using PaddleOCR and LLM-based extraction.

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.10+-blue.svg)
![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-0.100+-green.svg)
![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-19+-61DAFB.svg)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)

---

## ✨ Features

- **🔍 Dual Extraction Modes**
  - **Rules-Based**: Fast, deterministic extraction using regex and heuristics
  - **LLM-Based**: Semantic extraction using local Llama 3.2 via Ollama
  
- **🖼️ Image Preprocessing**: Grayscale, adaptive thresholding, deskewing

- **🌐 Full-Stack Application**
  - FastAPI backend with REST endpoints
  - React frontend with drag-and-drop upload
  - Side-by-side comparison view

- **🔒 100% Local**: No cloud APIs, all processing on your machine

---

## 🚀 Quick Start

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.10+
- Node.js 18+
- [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) (Python package manager)
- [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) with `llama3.2` model

### Installation

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/jeffersonqiu/llm_ocr.git
cd llm_ocr

# Install Python dependencies
uv sync

# Install frontend dependencies
cd web && npm install && cd ..
```

### Running the Application

**1. Start the Backend API**
```bash
uv run uvicorn api.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

**2. Start the Frontend** (in a new terminal)
```bash
cd web && npm run dev
```

**3. Open your browser**
- Frontend: http://localhost:5173
- API Docs: http://localhost:8000/docs

---

#### Source: `src/extractor_llm.py`

````py
import json
import re
import ollama
from typing import Dict, Any, Optional


class ReceiptLLM:
    """
    LLM wrapper for receipt data extraction using local Ollama models.
    """

    SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
You are an expert receipt parser specialising in US grocery and retail receipts.

Your task: extract structured data from OCR text of a receipt and return ONLY valid JSON.
No markdown code fences. No explanation. No commentary. Just the raw JSON object.

--- Receipt format notes ---
• Item lines look like:  ITEM NAME   UPC-CODE   PRICE  FLAG
  - UPC-CODE: a long (8–14 digit) barcode number — IGNORE it.
  - FLAG: a 1–2 letter suffix after the price (X, N, F, O, KI, B, H …) — IGNORE it.
    X = taxable, N = non-taxable, F = food-exempt, O = other. They are NOT part of the price.
  - PRICE: the dollar amount immediately before the flag (e.g. "1.97", "19.77").
  - COUPON lines reduce the total — include them as negative-price items.
• Date often appears near the bottom as  MM/DD/YY  (e.g. "07/28/17" = 2017-07-28).
• SUBTOTAL ≠ TOTAL. Use the TOTAL (or VISA TEND amount) as the grand total.
• If a field cannot be determined, use null.

--- JSON schema (return exactly this shape) ---
{
  "vendor": "string or null",
  "date": "YYYY-MM-DD or null",
  "total": number or null,
  "items": [
    {"name": "string", "price": number}
  ]
}

--- Example ---
Receipt text:
  Walmart
  07/28/17  02:39:48
  PET TOY  004747571846  1.97 X
  COUPON 23100  52310037000  -1.00 O
  SUBTOTAL  93.62
  TAX 1  6.750 %  4.59
  TOTAL  98.21
  VISA TEND  98.21

Expected JSON:
{
  "vendor": "Walmart",
  "date": "2017-07-28",
  "total": 98.21,
  "items": [
    {"name": "PET TOY", "price": 1.97},
    {"name": "COUPON 23100", "price": -1.00}
  ]
}
"""

    def __init__(self, model_name: str = "llama3.2"):
        self.model_name = model_name

    def extract(self, ocr_text: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Extract structured data from raw OCR text using the local LLM.
        """
        try:
            response = ollama.chat(
                model=self.model_name,
                messages=[
                    {'role': 'system', 'content': self.SYSTEM_PROMPT},
                    {'role': 'user',   'content': self._build_user_prompt(ocr_text)},
                ],
                options={
                    'temperature': 0.0,   # Deterministic — no creative hallucination
                    'num_predict': 2048,  # Allow enough tokens for long receipts
                }
            )
            content = response['message']['content']
            return self._parse_json(content)

        except Exception as e:
            print(f"LLM Extraction failed: {e}")
            return {}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _build_user_prompt(self, text: str) -> str:
        return (
            "Receipt text (from OCR — may contain minor misreads):\n\n"
            f"{text}\n\n"
            "Extract the data and return ONLY the JSON object."
        )

    def _parse_json(self, response_text: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Robustly parse JSON from LLM response.

        Attempts (in order):
        1. Strip markdown fences and parse directly.
        2. Find the first '{...}' block and parse that.
        3. Return empty dict.
        """
        s = response_text.strip()

        # Remove markdown code fences
        s = re.sub(r'^```(?:json)?\s*', '', s)
        s = re.sub(r'\s*```$', '', s.strip())
        s = s.strip()

        # Attempt 1: direct parse
        try:
            return json.loads(s)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            pass

        # Attempt 2: find first JSON object in the response
        m = re.search(r'\{.*\}', s, re.DOTALL)
        if m:
            try:
                return json.loads(m.group(0))
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                pass

        print(f"[LLM] Failed to parse JSON. Raw output:\n{response_text[:500]}")
        return {}

````

````py
import re
import statistics
from typing import List, Dict, Optional, Any
from dateutil import parser as dateutil_parser


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constants
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_SKIP_ROW_KEYWORDS = {
    'subtotal', 'sub total', 'sub-total',
    'tax', 'hst', 'gst', 'pst', 'vat',
    'total', 'grand total', 'amount due', 'balance due',
    'tend', 'cash', 'change', 'debit', 'credit', 'visa', 'mastercard',
    'approval', 'ref #', 'ref#', 'trans id', 'trans #',
    'terminal', 'tc#', 'tc #', 'aid', 'validation', 'payment service',
    'change due', 'items sold', '# items',
    'st#', 'op#', 'te#', 'tr#',
    'manager', 'save money', 'low price', 'customer copy',
    'coupon', 'signature',
}

# Walmart trailing tax/flag chars after prices ("1.97 X", "5.47 N")
_WALMART_FLAGS = re.compile(r'^[XNFOIBHEKIKT]{1,2}$', re.IGNORECASE)

# UPC / item-code: 6+ digits optionally followed by 1-3 uppercase letters (e.g. 00000000004614KI)
_UPC_PATTERN = re.compile(r'^\d{6,}[A-Z]{0,3}$', re.IGNORECASE)

# Standalone price token (bare number, optional currency prefix)
_AMOUNT_RE = re.compile(r'^[\$£€]?\s*(\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*(?:\.\d{1,2})?)$')

# Amount anywhere in a line
_AMOUNT_IN_LINE_RE = re.compile(r'[\$£€]?\s*(\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*\.\d{2})')

# Trailing single-letter tax flags in assembled item names ("CALZONE F" → "CALZONE")
_TRAILING_FLAG_RE = re.compile(r'\s+[FNIOXBHEK]{1,2}$', re.IGNORECASE)


def _is_skip_row(text: str) -> bool:
    lower = text.lower()
    return any(kw in lower for kw in _SKIP_ROW_KEYWORDS)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Vendor
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def extract_vendor(lines: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
    IGNORE_WORDS = {'receipt', 'welcome', 'tax invoice', 'copy', 'payment'}
    for line in lines[:5]:
        text = line['text'].strip()
        if len(text) < 2:
            continue
        if any(w in text.lower() for w in IGNORE_WORDS):
            continue
        return text
    return "Unknown Vendor"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Date
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def extract_date(lines: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Extract transaction date and return ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD).
    Handles MM/DD/YY (most common on US receipts like Walmart 07/28/17).
    """
    date_patterns = [
        (r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}',              False),   # ISO
        (r'\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{2}(?!\d)',    True),    # MM/DD/YY  ← Walmart
        (r'\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{4}',          False),   # MM/DD/YYYY
        (r'\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{4}',              False),   # DD-MM-YYYY
        (r'\d{1,2}\s+[A-Za-z]{3}\s+\d{4}', False),   # 28 Jul 2017
        (r'[A-Za-z]{3}\s+\d{1,2},?\s+\d{4}', False), # Jul 28, 2017
    ]

    texts = [line['text'] for line in lines]
    # Also scan adjacent-pair merges (OCR sometimes splits dates)
    extended = texts + [texts[i] + ' ' + texts[i + 1] for i in range(len(texts) - 1)]

    for text in extended:
        for pattern, is_2digit_year in date_patterns:
            m = re.search(pattern, text)
            if m:
                date_str = m.group(0)
                try:
                    if is_2digit_year:
                        dt = dateutil_parser.parse(date_str, dayfirst=False, yearfirst=False)
                        if dt.year > 2030:
                            dt = dt.replace(year=dt.year - 100)
                    else:
                        dt = dateutil_parser.parse(date_str, dayfirst=False)
                    return dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
                except (ValueError, OverflowError):
                    continue
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Total
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def extract_total(lines: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> float:
    def _amounts(text: str) -> List[float]:
        vals = []
        for m in _AMOUNT_IN_LINE_RE.finditer(text):
            try:
                vals.append(float(m.group(1).replace(',', '')))
            except ValueError:
                pass
        return vals

    # Pass 1: TOTAL keyword (not SUBTOTAL)
    candidates: List[float] = []
    for line in lines:
        lower = line['text'].lower()
        if re.search(r'\btotal\b', lower) and 'subtotal' not in lower and 'sub total' not in lower:
            candidates.extend(_amounts(line['text']))
    if candidates:
        return max(candidates)

    # Pass 2: TEND lines (Walmart payment tender)
    tend: List[float] = []
    for line in lines:
        if 'tend' in line['text'].lower():
            tend.extend(_amounts(line['text']))
    if tend:
        return max(tend)

    # Pass 3: largest amount in the bottom half
    all_amounts: List[float] = []
    for line in lines[len(lines) // 2:]:
        all_amounts.extend(_amounts(line['text']))
    return max(all_amounts) if all_amounts else 0.0


def extract_subtotal(lines: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> float:
    """
    Extract SUBTOTAL specifically (before-tax total).
    Returns 0.0 if not found.
    """
    for line in lines:
        lower = line['text'].lower()
        if 'subtotal' in lower or 'sub total' in lower or 'sub-total' in lower:
            for m in _AMOUNT_IN_LINE_RE.finditer(line['text']):
                try:
                    return float(m.group(1).replace(',', ''))
                except ValueError:
                    pass
    return 0.0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Price correction: fix OCR "0" → "8" misread
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _correct_prices(items: List[Dict[str, Any]], total: float,
                     subtotal: float = 0.0) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Post-process items to fix a common OCR error where "0.XX" is read as "8.XX".

    Strategy (combinatorial + heuristic):
    1. Identify all items whose price is 8.XX (8.00 ≤ p < 9.00).
    2. Enumerate all 2^n correction combos; pick combo closest to anchor
       (SUBTOTAL preferred, else TOTAL).
    3. Heuristic pass: if ≥3 items originally shared the same 8.XX price and
       the majority were corrected, correct the rest too.  This catches cases
       where missing items (coupons, items OCR failed to detect) throw off
       the subtotal-based combinatorial search.
    4. With ≤15 candidates this is at most 2^15 = 32768 iterations — instant.
    """
    anchor = subtotal if subtotal > 0 else total
    if anchor <= 0:
        return items

    corrected = [dict(i) for i in items]  # shallow copy

    # Find indices of 8.XX candidates
    candidates = [i for i, it in enumerate(corrected) if 8.0 <= it['price'] < 9.0]

    if not candidates:
        return corrected

    # Cap at 15 to keep combinatorial search tractable
    if len(candidates) > 15:
        candidates = candidates[:15]

    base_sum = sum(it['price'] for it in corrected)
    best_mask = 0          # bitmask of which candidates to correct
    best_delta = abs(base_sum - anchor)

    n = len(candidates)
    for mask in range(1, 1 << n):
        adjustment = 0.0
        for bit in range(n):
            if mask & (1 << bit):
                adjustment += 8.0   # each 8.XX → 0.XX saves exactly 8.00
        new_sum = base_sum - adjustment
        delta = abs(new_sum - anchor)
        if delta < best_delta:
            best_delta = delta
            best_mask = mask

    # Apply the best correction
    corrected_indices = set()
    for bit in range(n):
        if best_mask & (1 << bit):
            idx = candidates[bit]
            corrected[idx]['price'] = round(corrected[idx]['price'] - 8.0, 2)
            corrected_indices.add(idx)

    # --- Heuristic pass ---
    # If ≥3 items shared the same original 8.XX price and majority were corrected,
    # correct any remaining ones too (OCR almost never misreads the same
    # digit differently across identical items).

    # Group candidates by their original 8.XX price
    price_groups: Dict[float, list] = {}
    for idx in candidates:
        p = items[idx]['price']
        price_groups.setdefault(p, []).append(idx)

    for price_val, group_indices in price_groups.items():
        if len(group_indices) < 3:
            continue
        num_corrected = sum(1 for idx in group_indices if idx in corrected_indices)
        # If majority were corrected, correct the rest
        if num_corrected >= len(group_indices) // 2:
            for idx in group_indices:
                if idx not in corrected_indices:
                    corrected[idx]['price'] = round(items[idx]['price'] - 8.0, 2)
                    corrected_indices.add(idx)

    return corrected


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Item extraction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def extract_items(lines: List[Dict[str, Any]], total: float = 0.0,
                  subtotal: float = 0.0) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Extract line items:
    1. Adaptive Y-tolerance grouping
    2. Strip UPC codes (incl. alphanumeric like 00000000004614KI) and Walmart tax flags
    3. Strip trailing flag letters from assembled name ("CALZONE F" → "CALZONE")
    4. Post-process prices to correct OCR 0→8 misread
    """
    if not lines:
        return []

    # Adaptive line height
    heights = [abs(l['bbox'][3] - l['bbox'][1]) for l in lines if l['bbox'][3] > l['bbox'][1]]
    line_height = statistics.median(heights) if heights else 20.0
    tolerance   = line_height * 0.55

    # Group tokens into rows
    rows: List[List[Dict]] = []
    current_row = [lines[0]]
    for token in lines[1:]:
        if abs(token['center_y'] - current_row[-1]['center_y']) <= tolerance:
            current_row.append(token)
        else:
            rows.append(current_row)
            current_row = [token]
    rows.append(current_row)

    items: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

    for row in rows:
        row_sorted = sorted(row, key=lambda t: t['bbox'][0])
        full_text = ' '.join(t['text'] for t in row_sorted)

        if _is_skip_row(full_text):
            continue

        # Remove UPC codes (long numeric or alphanumeric codes)
        meaningful = [t for t in row_sorted if not _UPC_PATTERN.match(t['text'])]

        # Remove trailing Walmart tax/flag tokens (X, N, F, O, KI …)
        while meaningful and _WALMART_FLAGS.match(meaningful[-1]['text']):
            meaningful.pop()

        if len(meaningful) < 2:
            continue

        # Last token should be the price
        last_token  = meaningful[-1]['text']
        price_match = _AMOUNT_RE.match(last_token)

        if not price_match:
            continue

        price_str = price_match.group(1).replace(',', '')
        try:
            price = float(price_str)
        except ValueError:
            continue

        # Build name from remaining tokens (also strip any UPCs that slipped through)
        name_tokens = [t for t in meaningful[:-1] if not _UPC_PATTERN.match(t['text'])]
        name = ' '.join(t['text'] for t in name_tokens).strip()

        # Strip trailing single-letter tax flags from the assembled name
        # e.g. "CALZONE F" → "CALZONE", "3 ORANGES F" → "3 ORANGES"
        name = _TRAILING_FLAG_RE.sub('', name).strip()

        if not name:
            continue

        # Safety guard: skip summary rows that slipped past keyword filter
        if any(kw in name.lower() for kw in ('total', 'tax', 'subtotal')):
            continue

        # Skip implausible prices (barcodes misread as prices)
        if price > 9999:
            continue

        items.append({'item_name': name, 'price': price})

    # Post-process: correct OCR 0→8 price misread using subtotal/total as anchor
    items = _correct_prices(items, total, subtotal=subtotal)

    return items


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main entry point
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def extract_receipt_data(ocr_results: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Main entry point for rules-based extraction."""
    vendor   = extract_vendor(ocr_results)
    date     = extract_date(ocr_results)
    total    = extract_total(ocr_results)
    subtotal = extract_subtotal(ocr_results)
    items    = extract_items(ocr_results, total=total, subtotal=subtotal)

    return {
        'vendor': vendor,
        'date':   date,
        'total':  total,
        'items':  items,
    }

````

````py
import cv2
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Tuple, Union


def deskew(image: np.ndarray) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, float]:
    """
    Detect skew angle and rotate image to correct it.

    Uses Hough Line Transform to find dominant lines,
    then calculates the median angle.
    """
    # Invert for edge detection (text becomes white)
    inverted = cv2.bitwise_not(image)

    # Detect edges
    edges = cv2.Canny(inverted, 50, 150, apertureSize=3)

    # Detect lines using Hough Transform
    lines = cv2.HoughLinesP(edges, 1, np.pi / 180, 100, minLineLength=100, maxLineGap=10)

    if lines is None:
        return image, 0.0

    # Calculate angles of detected lines
    angles = []
    for line in lines:
        x1, y1, x2, y2 = line[0]
        angle = np.degrees(np.arctan2(y2 - y1, x2 - x1))
        # Only consider near-horizontal lines
        if abs(angle) < 45:
            angles.append(angle)

    if not angles:
        return image, 0.0

    # Use median angle to reduce outlier impact
    median_angle = np.median(angles)

    # Only correct if skew is meaningful (avoid over-rotating already-straight images)
    if abs(median_angle) < 0.5:
        return image, 0.0

    # Rotate image to correct skew
    (h, w) = image.shape[:2]
    center = (w // 2, h // 2)
    M = cv2.getRotationMatrix2D(center, median_angle, 1.0)
    rotated = cv2.warpAffine(image, M, (w, h), flags=cv2.INTER_CUBIC,
                              borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE)

    return rotated, float(median_angle)


def preprocess_receipt(image_path: Union[str, Path], scale_factor: float = 1.5) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Complete preprocessing pipeline for receipt images.

    Pipeline:
    1. Load & convert to grayscale
    2. CLAHE — boosts faded thermal ink without over-saturating
    3. Gentle Gaussian blur — removes scanner/camera noise
    4. Otsu thresholding — optimal global binarization for high-contrast receipts
    5. Morphological closing — reconnects broken character strokes
    6. Upscale 1.5× (INTER_CUBIC) — gives PaddleOCR more pixel resolution
    7. Deskew — corrects camera tilt

    Args:
        image_path: Path to the receipt image
        scale_factor: Upscale factor (default 2.0×)

    Returns:
        Preprocessed binary image as numpy array (uint8)
    """
    # 1. Load image
    img = cv2.imread(str(image_path))
    if img is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not load image: {image_path}")

    # 2. Convert to grayscale
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)

    # 3. CLAHE — Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization
    #    clipLimit=2.0 and tileGridSize=8×8 work well for receipt paper textures
    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=2.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)

    # 4. Gentle Gaussian blur to suppress sensor/JPEG noise before thresholding
    blurred = cv2.GaussianBlur(enhanced, (3, 3), 0)

    # 5. Otsu thresholding — automatically finds the optimal global threshold
    #    Works excellently on high-contrast thermal receipt prints
    _, binary = cv2.threshold(blurred, 0, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY + cv2.THRESH_OTSU)

    # 6. Morphological closing — reconnects strokes broken by Otsu binarization
    #    Kernel (2,1): vertical closing only to avoid merging adjacent characters horizontally
    kernel = cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_RECT, (2, 1))
    closed = cv2.morphologyEx(binary, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel)

    # 7. Upscale — 2× gives PaddleOCR significantly more pixels to work with
    width = int(closed.shape[1] * scale_factor)
    height = int(closed.shape[0] * scale_factor)
    upscaled = cv2.resize(closed, (width, height), interpolation=cv2.INTER_CUBIC)

    # 8. Deskew
    deskewed, _ = deskew(upscaled)

    return deskewed


def preprocess_receipt_raw(image_path: Union[str, Path], scale_factor: float = 2.0) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Lighter preprocessing: grayscale + CLAHE + upscale only (no binarization).

    Use as a fallback when Otsu binarization degrades OCR quality on
    colour photos or low-contrast scans.

    Args:
        image_path: Path to the receipt image
        scale_factor: Upscale factor (default 2.0×)

    Returns:
        Grayscale enhanced image as numpy array (uint8)
    """
    img = cv2.imread(str(image_path))
    if img is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not load image: {image_path}")

    gray = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)

    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=2.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)

    width = int(enhanced.shape[1] * scale_factor)
    height = int(enhanced.shape[0] * scale_factor)
    upscaled = cv2.resize(enhanced, (width, height), interpolation=cv2.INTER_CUBIC)

    deskewed, _ = deskew(upscaled)
    return deskewed

````

#### Source: `src/ocr_engine.py`

````py
from paddleocr import PaddleOCR
import cv2
import os
import statistics
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Dict, Union


class ReceiptOCR:
    """
    OCR wrapper for receipt images (PaddleOCR v3.x).

    Usage:
        ocr = ReceiptOCR()
        results = ocr.process("path/to/receipt.jpg")   # or numpy array
        text    = ocr.get_full_text(results)
    """

    def __init__(self, lang: str = 'en'):
        os.environ['PADDLE_PDX_DISABLE_MODEL_SOURCE_CHECK'] = 'True'

        self.engine = PaddleOCR(
            use_textline_orientation=False,  # We already deskew — skipping saves ~30% time
            enable_mkldnn=False,             # Avoid unsupported oneDNN PIR attrs on Windows
            lang=lang,
        )

    def process(self, image: Union[str, Path, np.ndarray]) -> List[Dict]:
        """
        Run OCR on an image (file path OR pre-loaded numpy array) and return
        parsed, sorted results.

        Accepting numpy arrays avoids a disk round-trip when the caller has
        already preprocessed the image in memory.

        Note: PaddleOCR v3.x requires 3-channel BGR images internally.
              Grayscale arrays are automatically converted here.

        Returns:
            List of dicts: text, confidence, bbox [x1,y1,x2,y2], center_y, center_x
        """
        if isinstance(image, Path):
            src = str(image)
        elif isinstance(image, np.ndarray):
            # PaddleOCR v3.x internal pipeline requires 3-channel BGR —
            # convert grayscale (H, W) or single-channel (H, W, 1) to BGR
            if image.ndim == 2:
                src = cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR)
            elif image.ndim == 3 and image.shape[2] == 1:
                src = cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR)
            else:
                src = image  # already BGR
        else:
            src = image  # string path

        results = self.engine.ocr(src)
        return self._parse_results(results)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Public helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def get_full_text(self, parsed_results: List[Dict]) -> str:
        """
        Reconstruct the receipt as a human-readable string preserving
        the two-column layout (item name left, price right).

        Args:
            parsed_results: Output of process()

        Returns:
            Multi-line string suitable for feeding to an LLM.
        """
        rows = self._group_into_rows(parsed_results)
        lines = []
        for row in rows:
            row_sorted = sorted(row, key=lambda t: t['bbox'][0])
            lines.append("  ".join(t['text'] for t in row_sorted))
        return "\n".join(lines)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Internal parsing helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _parse_results(self, results) -> List[Dict]:
        """Parse raw PaddleOCR v3.x output into a clean, sorted token list."""
        parsed = []

        if not results or results[0] is None:
            return parsed

        page_result = results[0]

        # ---------- PaddleOCR v3.x dict-like format ----------
        if 'rec_texts' in page_result:
            texts  = page_result['rec_texts']
            scores = page_result['rec_scores']
            boxes  = page_result['rec_boxes']   # ndarray (N, 4)

            for i in range(len(texts)):
                text = texts[i].strip()
                if not text:
                    continue

                confidence = scores[i]
                box = boxes[i]
                x1, y1, x2, y2 = float(box[0]), float(box[1]), float(box[2]), float(box[3])
                center_y = (y1 + y2) / 2
                center_x = (x1 + x2) / 2

                parsed.append({
                    'text':       text,
                    'confidence': round(confidence, 3),
                    'bbox':       [round(x1), round(y1), round(x2), round(y2)],
                    'center_y':   round(center_y, 1),
                    'center_x':   round(center_x, 1),
                })

        # ---------- Legacy format fallback (PaddleOCR v2.x) ----------
        else:
            for line in page_result:
                bbox_points = line[0]
                text, confidence = line[1]
                text = text.strip()
                if not text:
                    continue

                x_coords = [p[0] for p in bbox_points]
                y_coords = [p[1] for p in bbox_points]
                x1, x2 = min(x_coords), max(x_coords)
                y1, y2 = min(y_coords), max(y_coords)
                center_y = (y1 + y2) / 2
                center_x = (x1 + x2) / 2

                parsed.append({
                    'text':       text,
                    'confidence': round(float(confidence), 3),
                    'bbox':       [round(x1), round(y1), round(x2), round(y2)],
                    'center_y':   round(center_y, 1),
                    'center_x':   round(center_x, 1),
                })

        parsed.sort(key=lambda t: (t['center_y'], t['center_x']))
        return parsed

    def _compute_line_height(self, tokens: List[Dict]) -> float:
        heights = [abs(t['bbox'][3] - t['bbox'][1]) for t in tokens
                   if t['bbox'][3] > t['bbox'][1]]
        if not heights:
            return 20.0
        return statistics.median(heights)

    def _group_into_rows(self, tokens: List[Dict]) -> List[List[Dict]]:
        """Group tokens into visual rows using an adaptive Y-tolerance (55% of median line height)."""
        if not tokens:
            return []

        tolerance = self._compute_line_height(tokens) * 0.55

        rows: List[List[Dict]] = []
        current_row = [tokens[0]]

        for token in tokens[1:]:
            if abs(token['center_y'] - current_row[-1]['center_y']) <= tolerance:
                current_row.append(token)
            else:
                rows.append(current_row)
                current_row = [token]

        rows.append(current_row)
        return rows

````

import requests
from pathlib import Path
import time

API_URL = "http://localhost:8000"
IMAGE_PATH = Path("images/receipt-ocr-original.jpg")

def test_health():
    try:
        r = requests.get(f"{API_URL}/health")
        print(f"Health: {r.status_code} - {r.json()}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Health Check Failed: {e}")

def test_analyze_rules():
    print("\nTesting /analyze/rules ...")
    start = time.time()
    try:
        with open(IMAGE_PATH, "rb") as f:
            files = {"file": f}
            r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/analyze/rules", files=files)
            print(f"Status: {r.status_code}")
            if r.status_code == 200:
                print(f"Response: {r.json()}")
            else:
                print(f"Error: {r.text}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Rules Test Failed: {e}")
    print(f"Time taken: {time.time() - start:.2f}s")

def test_analyze_llm():
    print("\nTesting /analyze/llm ...")
    start = time.time()
    try:
        with open(IMAGE_PATH, "rb") as f:
            files = {"file": f}
            # verify=False for local
            r = requests.post(f"{API_URL}/analyze/llm", files=files)
            print(f"Status: {r.status_code}")
            if r.status_code == 200:
                print(f"Response: {r.json()}")
            else:
                print(f"Error: {r.text}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"LLM Test Failed: {e}")
    print(f"Time taken: {time.time() - start:.2f}s")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_health()
    test_analyze_rules()
    # Uncomment to test LLM
    test_analyze_llm()

#### Source: `web/src/App.jsx`

````jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import axios from 'axios'
import './App.css'

const API_URL = 'http://localhost:8000'

function App() {
  const [image, setImage] = useState(null)
  const [imagePreview, setImagePreview] = useState(null)
  const [mode, setMode] = useState('rules') // 'rules' | 'llm' | 'compare'
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)
  const [result, setResult] = useState(null)
  const [compareResults, setCompareResults] = useState({ rules: null, llm: null })
  const [error, setError] = useState(null)
  const [responseTime, setResponseTime] = useState(null)
  const [dragOver, setDragOver] = useState(false)

  const handleFileSelect = (file) => {
    if (file && file.type.startsWith('image/')) {
      setImage(file)
      setImagePreview(URL.createObjectURL(file))
      setResult(null)
      setCompareResults({ rules: null, llm: null })
      setError(null)
    }
  }

  const handleDrop = (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setDragOver(false)
    const file = e.dataTransfer.files[0]
    handleFileSelect(file)
  }

  const handleDragOver = (e) => {
    e.preventDefault()
    setDragOver(true)
  }

  const handleDragLeave = () => setDragOver(false)

  const handleInputChange = (e) => {
    handleFileSelect(e.target.files[0])
  }

  const analyzeImage = async () => {
    if (!image) return

    setLoading(true)
    setError(null)
    const startTime = Date.now()

    try {
      if (mode === 'compare') {
        // Run both endpoints in parallel
        const formData1 = new FormData()
        formData1.append('file', image)
        const formData2 = new FormData()
        formData2.append('file', image)

        const [rulesRes, llmRes] = await Promise.all([
          axios.post(`${API_URL}/analyze/rules`, formData1),
          axios.post(`${API_URL}/analyze/llm`, formData2)
        ])

        setCompareResults({
          rules: rulesRes.data,
          llm: llmRes.data
        })
        setResult(null)
      } else {
        const formData = new FormData()
        formData.append('file', image)
        
        const endpoint = mode === 'rules' ? '/analyze/rules' : '/analyze/llm'
        const response = await axios.post(`${API_URL}${endpoint}`, formData)
        
        setResult(response.data)
        setCompareResults({ rules: null, llm: null })
      }

      setResponseTime(((Date.now() - startTime) / 1000).toFixed(2))
    } catch (err) {
      setError(err.response?.data?.detail || err.message)
    } finally {
      setLoading(false)
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="app">
      <header className="header">
        <h1>📄 Receipt OCR</h1>
        <p>Extract data from receipts using AI-powered OCR</p>
      </header>

      <div className="main-content">
        {/* Left Panel - Upload & Controls */}
        <div className="card">
          <h2>📤 Upload Receipt</h2>
          
          <div
            className={`upload-zone ${dragOver ? 'dragover' : ''} ${imagePreview ? 'has-image' : ''}`}
            onDrop={handleDrop}
            onDragOver={handleDragOver}
            onDragLeave={handleDragLeave}
            onClick={() => document.getElementById('file-input').click()}
          >
            {imagePreview ? (
              <img src={imagePreview} alt="Receipt preview" />
            ) : (
              <>
                <div className="upload-icon">📷</div>
                <p>Drag & drop an image or click to browse</p>
              </>
            )}
            <input
              type="file"
              id="file-input"
              accept="image/*"
              onChange={handleInputChange}
              style={{ display: 'none' }}
            />
          </div>

          <div className="mode-selector">
            <button
              className={`mode-btn ${mode === 'rules' ? 'active' : ''}`}
              onClick={() => setMode('rules')}
            >
              ⚡ Rules
            </button>
            <button
              className={`mode-btn ${mode === 'llm' ? 'active' : ''}`}
              onClick={() => setMode('llm')}
            >
              🤖 LLM
            </button>
            <button
              className={`mode-btn ${mode === 'compare' ? 'active' : ''}`}
              onClick={() => setMode('compare')}
            >
              ⚖️ Compare
            </button>
          </div>

          <button
            className="analyze-btn"
            onClick={analyzeImage}
            disabled={!image || loading}
          >
            {loading ? (
              <>
                <span className="spinner"></span>
                Analyzing...
              </>
            ) : (
              <>🔍 Analyze Receipt</>
            )}
          </button>

          {error && (
            <div className="error-message">
              ❌ {error}
            </div>
          )}
        </div>

        {/* Right Panel - Results */}
        <div className="card results-panel">
          <h2>📊 Results</h2>
          
          {mode === 'compare' && (compareResults.rules || compareResults.llm) ? (
            <CompareView 
              rules={compareResults.rules} 
              llm={compareResults.llm}
              responseTime={responseTime}
            />
          ) : result ? (
            <ResultsView data={result} mode={mode} responseTime={responseTime} />
          ) : (
            <div className="empty-state">
              <p>Upload an image and click Analyze to see results</p>
            </div>
          )}
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

function ResultsView({ data, mode, responseTime }) {
  return (
    <>
      <div className="result-header">
        <span className="result-badge">{mode === 'rules' ? '⚡ Rules' : '🤖 LLM'}</span>
        <span className="result-time">⏱️ {responseTime}s</span>
      </div>

      <div className="result-field">
        <label>Vendor</label>
        <div className="value">{data.vendor || 'Unknown'}</div>
      </div>

      <div className="result-field">
        <label>Date</label>
        <div className="value">{data.date || 'Not detected'}</div>
      </div>

      <div className="result-field">
        <label>Total</label>
        <div className="value large">${data.total?.toFixed(2) || '0.00'}</div>
      </div>

      {data.items && data.items.length > 0 && (
        <div className="result-field">
          <label>Items ({data.items.length})</label>
          <table className="items-table">
            <thead>
              <tr>
                <th>Item</th>
                <th className="price">Price</th>
              </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
              {data.items.map((item, i) => (
                <tr key={i}>
                  <td>{item.item_name}</td>
                  <td className="price">${item.price?.toFixed(2)}</td>
                </tr>
              ))}
            </tbody>
          </table>
        </div>
      )}
    </>
  )
}

function CompareView({ rules, llm, responseTime }) {
  return (
    <>
      <div className="result-header">
        <span className="result-badge">⚖️ Compare</span>
        <span className="result-time">⏱️ {responseTime}s</span>
      </div>

      <div className="compare-container">
        <div className="compare-panel">
          <h3>⚡ Rules-Based</h3>
          {rules && (
            <>
              <p><strong>Vendor:</strong> {rules.vendor}</p>
              <p><strong>Date:</strong> {rules.date || 'N/A'}</p>
              <p><strong>Total:</strong> ${rules.total?.toFixed(2)}</p>
              <p><strong>Items:</strong> {rules.items?.length || 0}</p>
            </>
          )}
        </div>

        <div className="compare-panel">
          <h3>🤖 LLM-Based</h3>
          {llm && (
            <>
              <p><strong>Vendor:</strong> {llm.vendor}</p>
              <p><strong>Date:</strong> {llm.date || 'N/A'}</p>
              <p><strong>Total:</strong> ${llm.total?.toFixed(2)}</p>
              <p><strong>Items:</strong> {llm.items?.length || 0}</p>
            </>
          )}
        </div>
      </div>
    </>
  )
}

export default App

````
