:root {
  --bg-primary: #0f0f1a;
  --bg-secondary: #1a1a2e;
  --bg-glass: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05);
  --text-primary: #ffffff;
  --text-secondary: #a0a0b0;
  --accent: #6366f1;
  --accent-hover: #818cf8;
  --success: #10b981;
  --border: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1);
  --shadow: 0 8px 32px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3);
}

* {
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

body {
  font-family: 'Inter', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, sans-serif;
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--bg-primary) 0%, #16213e 100%);
  color: var(--text-primary);
  min-height: 100vh;
}

.app {
  max-width: 1400px;
  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 2rem;
}

.header {
  text-align: center;
  margin-bottom: 3rem;
}

.header h1 {
  font-size: 2.5rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #fff 0%, #a0a0ff 100%);
  -webkit-background-clip: text;
  -webkit-text-fill-color: transparent;
  background-clip: text;
  margin-bottom: 0.5rem;
}

.header p {
  color: var(--text-secondary);
  font-size: 1.1rem;
}

.main-content {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
  gap: 2rem;
}

@media (max-width: 900px) {
  .main-content {
    grid-template-columns: 1fr;
  }
}

/* Glass Card */
.card {
  background: var(--bg-glass);
  backdrop-filter: blur(20px);
  border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: 16px;
  padding: 1.5rem;
  box-shadow: var(--shadow);
}

.card h2 {
  font-size: 1.25rem;
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.5rem;
}

/* Upload Zone */
.upload-zone {
  border: 2px dashed var(--border);
  border-radius: 12px;
  padding: 3rem 2rem;
  text-align: center;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: all 0.3s ease;
  background: var(--bg-secondary);
}

.upload-zone:hover, .upload-zone.dragover {
  border-color: var(--accent);
  background: rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.1);
}

.upload-zone.has-image {
  padding: 1rem;
}

.upload-zone img {
  max-width: 100%;
  max-height: 300px;
  border-radius: 8px;
  object-fit: contain;
}

.upload-icon {
  font-size: 3rem;
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
}

.upload-zone p {
  color: var(--text-secondary);
}

/* Mode Selector */
.mode-selector {
  display: flex;
  gap: 0.5rem;
  margin: 1.5rem 0;
}

.mode-btn {
  flex: 1;
  padding: 0.75rem 1rem;
  border: 1px solid var(--border);
  background: var(--bg-secondary);
  color: var(--text-secondary);
  border-radius: 8px;
  cursor: pointer;
  font-size: 0.9rem;
  font-weight: 500;
  transition: all 0.3s ease;
}

.mode-btn:hover {
  background: rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.1);
  color: var(--text-primary);
}

.mode-btn.active {
  background: var(--accent);
  border-color: var(--accent);
  color: white;
}

/* Analyze Button */
.analyze-btn {
  width: 100%;
  padding: 1rem;
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--accent) 0%, #8b5cf6 100%);
  color: white;
  border: none;
  border-radius: 10px;
  font-size: 1rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: all 0.3s ease;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  gap: 0.5rem;
}

.analyze-btn:hover:not(:disabled) {
  transform: translateY(-2px);
  box-shadow: 0 8px 20px rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.4);
}

.analyze-btn:disabled {
  opacity: 0.5;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}

/* Loading Spinner */
.spinner {
  width: 20px;
  height: 20px;
  border: 2px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.3);
  border-top-color: white;
  border-radius: 50%;
  animation: spin 0.8s linear infinite;
}

@keyframes spin {
  to { transform: rotate(360deg); }
}

/* Results */
.results-panel {
  min-height: 400px;
}

.result-header {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
  align-items: center;
  padding-bottom: 1rem;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
}

.result-badge {
  padding: 0.25rem 0.75rem;
  background: var(--success);
  color: white;
  border-radius: 20px;
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  font-weight: 600;
}

.result-time {
  color: var(--text-secondary);
  font-size: 0.85rem;
}

.result-field {
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
}

.result-field label {
  display: block;
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  color: var(--text-secondary);
  text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: 0.05em;
  margin-bottom: 0.25rem;
}

.result-field .value {
  font-size: 1.1rem;
  font-weight: 500;
}

.result-field .value.large {
  font-size: 1.5rem;
  color: var(--success);
}

/* Items Table */
.items-table {
  width: 100%;
  border-collapse: collapse;
  margin-top: 1rem;
}

.items-table th,
.items-table td {
  padding: 0.75rem;
  text-align: left;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
}

.items-table th {
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  color: var(--text-secondary);
  text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: 0.05em;
}

.items-table td {
  font-size: 0.9rem;
}

.items-table .price {
  text-align: right;
  font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;
}

/* Empty State */
.empty-state {
  text-align: center;
  padding: 3rem;
  color: var(--text-secondary);
}

.empty-state svg {
  width: 64px;
  height: 64px;
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
  opacity: 0.5;
}

/* Compare Mode Toggle */
.compare-toggle {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.5rem;
  margin-top: 1rem;
  padding: 0.75rem;
  background: var(--bg-secondary);
  border-radius: 8px;
  cursor: pointer;
}

.compare-toggle input {
  accent-color: var(--accent);
}

.compare-toggle label {
  cursor: pointer;
  font-size: 0.9rem;
}

/* Compare View */
.compare-container {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
  gap: 1rem;
}

.compare-panel {
  background: var(--bg-secondary);
  border-radius: 12px;
  padding: 1rem;
}

.compare-panel h3 {
  font-size: 0.9rem;
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
  padding-bottom: 0.5rem;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
}

/* Error State */
.error-message {
  background: rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.1);
  border: 1px solid rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.3);
  color: #fca5a5;
  padding: 1rem;
  border-radius: 8px;
  margin-top: 1rem;
}

````markdown
# 01 - Image Preprocessing for Receipt OCR

**Goal:** Prepare receipt images for better OCR accuracy

**Key Techniques:**
1. Grayscale conversion - Reduces complexity
2. Adaptive thresholding - Handles uneven lighting
3. Upscaling (1.5-2×) - Improves character recognition
4. Deskewing - Straightens rotated receipts

> **Why this matters:** OCR accuracy improves more from preprocessing than from model changes.
````

````markdown
## Step 3: Adaptive Thresholding

**Why adaptive (not global) thresholding?**
- Receipts often have uneven lighting
- Adaptive threshold calculates different thresholds for different regions
- Results in cleaner black/white separation
````

##### `notebooks/01_preprocessing.ipynb` cell 9: code; execution count `6`

````python
# Apply adaptive thresholding
# Parameters:
#   - maxValue: 255 (white)
#   - adaptiveMethod: ADAPTIVE_THRESH_GAUSSIAN_C (weighted mean of neighborhood)
#   - thresholdType: THRESH_BINARY (above threshold = white)
#   - blockSize: 11 (neighborhood size, must be odd)
#   - C: 2 (constant subtracted from mean)

thresh = cv2.adaptiveThreshold(
    gray, 
    255, 
    cv2.ADAPTIVE_THRESH_GAUSSIAN_C, 
    cv2.THRESH_BINARY, 
    11, 
    2
)

# Compare original gray vs thresholded
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 10))
axes[0].imshow(gray, cmap='gray')
axes[0].set_title("Grayscale")
axes[0].axis('off')

axes[1].imshow(thresh, cmap='gray')
axes[1].set_title("Adaptive Threshold")
axes[1].axis('off')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
````

````markdown
## Step 5: Deskewing (Optional)

**Why deskew?**
- Receipts are often photographed at an angle
- OCR works best on horizontal text
- We detect the dominant angle and rotate to correct
````

##### `notebooks/01_preprocessing.ipynb` cell 13: code; execution count `8`

````python
def deskew(image):
    """
    Detect skew angle and rotate image to correct it.
    
    Uses Hough Line Transform to find dominant lines,
    then calculates the median angle.
    """
    # Invert for edge detection (text becomes white)
    inverted = cv2.bitwise_not(image)
    
    # Detect edges
    edges = cv2.Canny(inverted, 50, 150, apertureSize=3)
    
    # Detect lines using Hough Transform
    lines = cv2.HoughLinesP(edges, 1, np.pi/180, 100, minLineLength=100, maxLineGap=10)
    
    if lines is None:
        print("No lines detected, skipping deskew")
        return image, 0
    
    # Calculate angles of detected lines
    angles = []
    for line in lines:
        x1, y1, x2, y2 = line[0]
        angle = np.degrees(np.arctan2(y2 - y1, x2 - x1))
        # Only consider near-horizontal lines
        if abs(angle) < 45:
            angles.append(angle)
    
    if not angles:
        print("No horizontal lines detected, skipping deskew")
        return image, 0
    
    # Use median angle to reduce outlier impact
    median_angle = np.median(angles)
    print(f"Detected skew angle: {median_angle:.2f}°")
    
    # Rotate image to correct skew
    (h, w) = image.shape[:2]
    center = (w // 2, h // 2)
    M = cv2.getRotationMatrix2D(center, median_angle, 1.0)
    rotated = cv2.warpAffine(image, M, (w, h), flags=cv2.INTER_CUBIC, 
                              borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE)
    
    return rotated, median_angle

# Apply deskewing
deskewed, angle = deskew(upscaled)
print(f"Applied rotation: {angle:.2f}°")
````

````markdown
## Complete Preprocessing Function

Here's the complete function we'll convert to a module later.
````

##### `notebooks/01_preprocessing.ipynb` cell 19: code; execution count `11`

````python
def preprocess_receipt(image_path: str, scale_factor: float = 1.5) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Complete preprocessing pipeline for receipt images.
    
    Args:
        image_path: Path to the receipt image
        scale_factor: How much to upscale (default 1.5x)
    
    Returns:
        Preprocessed image as numpy array
    """
    # Load image
    img = cv2.imread(str(image_path))
    if img is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not load image: {image_path}")
    
    # Convert to grayscale
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    
    # Adaptive thresholding
    thresh = cv2.adaptiveThreshold(
        gray, 255, 
        cv2.ADAPTIVE_THRESH_GAUSSIAN_C, 
        cv2.THRESH_BINARY, 
        11, 2
    )
    
    # Upscale
    width = int(thresh.shape[1] * scale_factor)
    height = int(thresh.shape[0] * scale_factor)
    upscaled = cv2.resize(thresh, (width, height), interpolation=cv2.INTER_CUBIC)
    
    # Deskew
    deskewed, _ = deskew(upscaled)
    
    return deskewed

# Test the complete function
if image_files:
    result = preprocess_receipt(image_files[0])
    print(f"✅ Preprocessing complete! Output shape: {result.shape}")
````

````markdown
## Step 5: Parse OCR Results into Clean Format

Let's create a structured representation of the OCR output.
````

##### `notebooks/02_ocr.ipynb` cell 13: code; execution count `17`

````python
def parse_ocr_results(results):
    """
    Parse PaddleOCR v3.x results into a clean list of dictionaries.
    
    Returns:
        List of dicts with: text, confidence, bbox (x1,y1,x2,y2), center_y
    """
    parsed = []
    
    if not results:
        return parsed
    
    result = results[0]  # First page
    texts = result['rec_texts']
    scores = result['rec_scores']
    polys = result['dt_polys']
    
    for i in range(len(texts)):
        bbox_points = polys[i]  # 4 corner points
        text = texts[i]
        confidence = scores[i]
        
        # Convert to simple bounding box (x1, y1, x2, y2)
        if hasattr(bbox_points, 'tolist'):
            bbox_points = bbox_points.tolist()
        x_coords = [p[0] for p in bbox_points]
        y_coords = [p[1] for p in bbox_points]
        
        x1, x2 = min(x_coords), max(x_coords)
        y1, y2 = min(y_coords), max(y_coords)
        
        # Center Y is useful for grouping lines
        center_y = (y1 + y2) / 2
        
        parsed.append({
            'text': text,
            'confidence': round(float(confidence), 3),
            'bbox': [round(x1), round(y1), round(x2), round(y2)],
            'center_y': round(center_y)
        })
    
    # Sort by Y coordinate (top to bottom)
    parsed.sort(key=lambda x: x['center_y'])
    
    return parsed

# Parse our results
parsed_results = parse_ocr_results(results)
print(f"Parsed {len(parsed_results)} text regions")
````

````markdown
## Step 6: Visualize OCR Results

Draw bounding boxes on the image to see what OCR detected.
````

##### `notebooks/02_ocr.ipynb` cell 16: code; execution count `19`

````python
def visualize_ocr(image_path, parsed_results, figsize=(12, 16)):
    """
    Draw bounding boxes and text on the image.
    """
    # Load image
    img = cv2.imread(str(image_path))
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=figsize)
    ax.imshow(img_rgb)
    
    # Draw each bounding box
    for item in parsed_results:
        x1, y1, x2, y2 = item['bbox']
        width = x2 - x1
        height = y2 - y1
        
        # Color based on confidence
        if item['confidence'] > 0.9:
            color = 'green'
        elif item['confidence'] > 0.7:
            color = 'orange'
        else:
            color = 'red'
        
        # Draw rectangle
        rect = patches.Rectangle(
            (x1, y1), width, height,
            linewidth=2, edgecolor=color, facecolor='none'
        )
        ax.add_patch(rect)
        
        # Add text label (small font)
        ax.text(x1, y1 - 5, item['text'][:20], fontsize=6, color=color)
    
    ax.set_title("OCR Results (Green=High, Orange=Medium, Red=Low confidence)")
    ax.axis('off')
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# Visualize
if image_files:
    visualize_ocr(image_path, parsed_results)
````

````markdown
## Step 7: Save Raw OCR Output (Important for Debugging!)

Always save the raw OCR output. When extraction rules fail, you'll want to inspect what OCR actually detected.
````

##### `notebooks/02_ocr.ipynb` cell 18: code; execution count `22`

````python
def save_ocr_results(parsed_results, image_path, output_dir):
    """
    Save OCR results as JSON for debugging.
    """
    output_path = Path(output_dir) / f"ocr_{Path(image_path).stem}.json"
    
    data = {
        'source_image': str(image_path),
        'num_regions': len(parsed_results),
        'results': parsed_results
    }
    
    with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
    
    print(f"✅ Saved OCR results to: {output_path}")
    return output_path

# Save results
if parsed_results:
    save_ocr_results(parsed_results, image_path, OUT_DIR)
````

##### `notebooks/02_ocr.ipynb` cell 21: code; execution count `21`

````python
class ReceiptOCR:
    """
    OCR wrapper for receipt images (PaddleOCR v3.x).
    
    Usage:
        ocr = ReceiptOCR()
        results = ocr.process("path/to/receipt.jpg")
    """
    
    def __init__(self, lang='en'):
        self.engine = PaddleOCR(
            use_textline_orientation=True,
            lang=lang
        )
    
    def process(self, image_path):
        """
        Run OCR on an image and return parsed results.
        
        Returns:
            List of dicts with: text, confidence, bbox, center_y
        """
        results = self.engine.predict(str(image_path))
        return self._parse_results(results)
    
    def _parse_results(self, results):
        """Parse raw PaddleOCR v3.x output into clean format."""
        parsed = []
        
        if not results:
            return parsed
        
        result = results[0]
        texts = result['rec_texts']
        scores = result['rec_scores']
        polys = result['dt_polys']
        
        for i in range(len(texts)):
            bbox_points = polys[i]
            if hasattr(bbox_points, 'tolist'):
                bbox_points = bbox_points.tolist()
            
            x_coords = [p[0] for p in bbox_points]
            y_coords = [p[1] for p in bbox_points]
            
            x1, x2 = min(x_coords), max(x_coords)
            y1, y2 = min(y_coords), max(y_coords)
            center_y = (y1 + y2) / 2
            
            parsed.append({
                'text': texts[i],
                'confidence': round(float(scores[i]), 3),
                'bbox': [round(x1), round(y1), round(x2), round(y2)],
                'center_y': round(center_y)
            })
        
        parsed.sort(key=lambda x: x['center_y'])
        return parsed

# Test the class
if image_files:
    receipt_ocr = ReceiptOCR()
    test_results = receipt_ocr.process(image_path)
    print(f"✅ ReceiptOCR class works! Detected {len(test_results)} text regions")
````

````markdown
# 03 - Rules-Based Data Extraction

**Goal:** Convert raw OCR text into structured data (vendor, date, total, items)

**Strategy:**
1. **Vendor:** First strong text line or largest text at top
2. **Date:** Regex matching for various date formats (YYYY-MM-DD, DD/MM/YYYY, etc.)
3. **Total:** Keyword search (TOTAL, AMOUNT, etc.) + currency parsing
4. **Items:** Clustering text by Y-coordinate rows

> **Why rules?** They are fast, deterministic, and easy to debug. LLMs are a fallback.
````

## Step 2: Extract Vendor

**Heuristic:** The vendor name is usually:
- At the very top
- High confidence
- Often excluding generic words like "Receipt", "Welcome", etc.
````

##### `notebooks/03_extraction.ipynb` cell 7: code; execution count `14`

````python
def extract_vendor(lines: List[Dict]) -> str:
    """
    Identify vendor name from top lines.
    Strategy: First line that isn't a generic header.
    """
    IGNORE_WORDS = {'receipt', 'welcome', 'tax invoice', 'copy', 'payment'}
    
    for line in lines[:5]:  # Look at top 5 lines
        text = line['text'].strip()
        clean_text = text.lower()
        
        # Skip empty or very short lines
        if len(text) < 2:
            continue
            
        # Skip lines containing ignore words
        if any(w in clean_text for w in IGNORE_WORDS):
            continue
            
        return text
    
    return "Unknown Vendor"

# Test it
vendor = extract_vendor(ocr_results)
print(f"Vendor: {vendor}")

## Step 3: Extract Date

**Heuristic:** Regex matching for common formats.
- `YYYY-MM-DD`
- `DD/MM/YYYY`
- `DD-MMM-YYYY`
````

##### `notebooks/03_extraction.ipynb` cell 9: code; execution count `15`

````python
def extract_date(lines: List[Dict]) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Extract date using regex matching.
    Returns ISO format date string (YYYY-MM-DD).
    """
    # Common date patterns
    date_patterns = [
        r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}',       # 2024-01-31
        r'\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}',       # 31/01/2024
        r'\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{4}',       # 31-01-2024
        r'\d{2}\s+[A-Za-z]{3}\s+\d{4}', # 31 Jan 2024
    ]
    
    for line in lines:
        text = line['text']
        for pattern in date_patterns:
            match = re.search(pattern, text)
            if match:
                date_str = match.group(0)
                try:
                    # Use dateutil parser to handle various formats
                    dt = parser.parse(date_str, dayfirst=True)
                    return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                    
    return None

# Test it
receipt_date = extract_date(ocr_results)
print(f"Date: {receipt_date}")
````

## Step 4: Extract Total Amount

**Heuristic:** Look for lines containing "Total" keywords, then extract the currency amount.
````

##### `notebooks/03_extraction.ipynb` cell 11: code; execution count `16`

````python
def extract_total(lines: List[Dict]) -> float:
    """
    Find total amount.
    Strategy: 
    1. Find lines with 'TOTAL', 'AMOUNT DUE', etc.
    2. Extract number from that line or the line immediately following (if right-aligned).
    """
    TOTAL_KEYWORDS = ['total', 'amount due', 'grand total', 'balance']
    
    # Regex for currency amount (e.g., $10.50, 10.50, 1,234.50)
    amount_re = r'[\$£€]?\s*(\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*(?:\.\d{2})?)'
    
    candidates = []
    
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        text = line['text'].lower()
        
        if any(k in text for k in TOTAL_KEYWORDS):
            # Try to find amount in same line
            matches = re.findall(amount_re, line['text'])
            if matches:
                # Take the last match (usually the final total)
                val = matches[-1].replace(',', '')
                try:
                    return float(val)
                except ValueError:
                    pass
            
            # If not in same line, check next line (common in OCR if spacing is wide)
            if i + 1 < len(lines):
                next_line = lines[i+1]['text']
                # Only if next line looks like a number
                matches = re.findall(amount_re, next_line)
                if matches:
                    val = matches[0].replace(',', '')
                    try:
                        return float(val)
                    except ValueError:
                        pass
                        
    return 0.0

# Test it
total_amount = extract_total(ocr_results)
print(f"Total: {total_amount}")

##### `notebooks/03_extraction.ipynb` cell 12: markdown; execution count `None`

````markdown
## Step 5: Extract Line Items (Advanced)

**Heuristic:** Group text by Y-coordinate.
Items usually consist of: `Name ....... Price`

We group OCR tokens that share roughly the same `center_y`.
````

##### `notebooks/03_extraction.ipynb` cell 13: code; execution count `17`

````python
def extract_items(lines: List[Dict], y_tolerance=10) -> List[Dict]:
    """
    Extract line items by grouping tokens into rows.
    """
    # 1. Group by Y-coordinate
    rows = []
    if not lines: 
        return []
    
    current_row = [lines[0]]
    
    for line in lines[1:]:
        prev_y = current_row[-1]['center_y']
        curr_y = line['center_y']
        
        if abs(curr_y - prev_y) <= y_tolerance:
            current_row.append(line)
        else:
            rows.append(current_row)
            current_row = [line]
    rows.append(current_row)
    
    # 2. Process each row to separate Item Name vs Price
    items = []
    amount_re = r'^\s*[\$£€]?\s*(\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*(?:\.\d{2})?)\s*$'
    
    for row in rows:
        # Sort by X coordinate (left to right)
        row.sort(key=lambda x: x['bbox'][0])
        
        row_text = " ".join([x['text'] for x in row])
        
        # Simple heuristic: Last token is price, rest is name
        # But check if last token matches number format
        last_token = row[-1]['text']
        match = re.match(amount_re, last_token)
        
        if match:
            price = float(match.group(1).replace(',', ''))
            name = " ".join([x['text'] for x in row[:-1]])
            
            # Filter out rows that are likely totals/subtotals
            if 'total' not in name.lower() and 'tax' not in name.lower() and name.strip():
                items.append({
                    'item_name': name,
                    'price': price
                })
                
    return items

# Test items
items = extract_items(ocr_results)
print(f"Found {len(items)} items:")
for item in items:
    print(f"  - {item['item_name']:<30}  {item['price']}")
````

##### `notebooks/03_extraction.ipynb` cell 14: markdown; execution count `None`

````markdown
## Analysis of Failures

**Observation:** You might notice errors in the item extraction above.
For example: `PET TOY` might show `7.00` instead of `1.97` if the columns aren't perfectly aligned or if the text is wrapped.

**Why this happens:**
- Simple Y-clustering assumes a straight horizontal line.
- It assumes the last number on the right is always the price.
- It fails when there's an internal code (like `040000000 7.00 G`) on the same line.

**Solution:** This is where a **Local LLM** shines. It understands context ("7.00 is likely a quantity or code, 1.97 is the price").

We will explore this in **Notebook 04**.
````

# 04 - LLM-Assisted Extraction

**Goal:** Use a local Large Language Model (Llama 3.2 3B) to intelligently parse OCR text.

**Why LLMs?** Rules are brittle. LLMs understand context (e.g., distinguishing a "quantity" from a "price" based on column position).

**Prerequisites:**
1. [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) installed and running.
2. Model pulled: `ollama pull llama3.2`
````

##### `notebooks/04_llm_extraction.ipynb` cell 6: code; execution count `20`

````python
def load_ocr_text(json_path):
    with open(json_path, 'r') as f:
        data = json.load(f)
        
    results = data.get('results', [])
    if not results: return ""
    
    # Sort by Y-center to preserve reading order
    # If 'center_y' key exists, use it to sort.
    if results and 'center_y' in results[0]:
        results.sort(key=lambda x: x['center_y'])
            
    # Create a single string representation
    text_lines = [item['text'] for item in results]
    return "\n".join(text_lines)

# Load first file
if OCR_JSON_FILES:
    json_path = OCR_JSON_FILES[0]
    ocr_text = load_ocr_text(json_path)
    print(f"Input Text ({len(ocr_text)} chars):\n---\n{ocr_text[:200]}...\n---")
````

````python
SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
You are an expert receipt parser. 
Extract structured data from the provided receipt text.
Return JSON only. No markdown formatting. No explanation.

JSON Schema:
{
    "vendor": "string",
    "date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
    "total": number,
    "items": [
        {"name": "string", "qty": number or null, "price": number}
    ]
}
"""

def build_user_prompt(text):
    return f"""Receipt Text:
{text}

Extract the data into JSON."""
````

##### `notebooks/04_llm_extraction.ipynb` cell 10: code; execution count `22`

def extract_with_llm(text):
    response = ollama.chat(model=MODEL_NAME, messages=[
        {'role': 'system', 'content': SYSTEM_PROMPT},
        {'role': 'user', 'content': build_user_prompt(text)},
    ])
    
    return response['message']['content']

# Run extraction
print("⏳ Asking Llama 3.2 to parse receipt...")
llm_response = extract_with_llm(ocr_text)
print("✅ Done!")

# Helper to clean markdown block format usually returned by LLMs
def clean_json_string(s):
    s = s.strip()
    if s.startswith("```json"):
        s = s[7:]
    if s.startswith("```"):
        s = s[3:]
    if s.endswith("```"):
        s = s[:-3]
    return s.strip()

# Parse JSON
data = {} # Initialize to avoid NameError
try:
    clean_response = clean_json_string(llm_response)
    data = json.loads(clean_response)
    print(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
except json.JSONDecodeError:
    print("❌ Failed to parse JSON. Raw output:")
    print(llm_response)
````

##### `notebooks/04_llm_extraction.ipynb` cell 15: markdown; execution count `None`

````markdown
---

## 🎯 Conclusion

**Local LLMs** are powerful for:
1.  **Handling structural noise** (e.g., ignoring random numbers on the line).
2.  **Contextual understanding** (knowing that "TAX" is not an item).
3.  **Zero-shot flexibility** (no regex tuning needed).

**Trade-off:** Slower than Rules/Regex, but much more robust for complex documents.
````

# 05 - Accuracy Benchmarking

**Goal:** Quantify the accuracy improvement of LLM vs Rules-Based extraction.

**Metrics:**
1. **Price Accuracy:** Exact match or within $0.01 tolerance (comparing `line_total` vs `price`).
2. **Name Accuracy:** Text similarity (Levenshtein distance) > 85%.
3. **Combined F1 Score:** Precision and Recall of extracted items.
````

##### `notebooks/05_benchmark.ipynb` cell 7: markdown; execution count `None`

````markdown
## Step 3: Define Scoring Function (Relaxed)

We updated the logic to handle:
1. **Substring matching**: If 'PET TOY' is in 'PET TOY 0047...', count it as match.
2. **Independent Price Scoring**: We also check how many price values match purely as a bag of numbers, ignoring alignment issues.
````

##### `notebooks/05_benchmark.ipynb` cell 8: code; execution count `18`

````python
def calculate_similarity(s1, s2):
    s1, s2 = str(s1).lower(), str(s2).lower()
    if not s1 or not s2: return 0.0
    # Handle substring case (e.g., 'PET TOY' in 'PET TOY 0047...')
    # We prioritize if GT name is inside extracted text
    if s2 in s1: return 1.0
    if s1 in s2: return 1.0 # Reverse check
    return SequenceMatcher(None, s1, s2).ratio()

def score_dataset(extracted_df, ground_truth_df, name_thresh=0.6):
    """
    Score extracted items against ground truth.
    """
    # Make copies to avoid modifying originals
    gt = ground_truth_df.copy()
    ext = extracted_df.copy()
    
    matches = []
    gt_matched = set()

    # 1. Matching Logic (Greedy)
    for i, row in ext.iterrows():
        best_j = -1
        best_score = 0.0
        
        # Iterate all GT items to find best match
        for j, gt_row in gt.iterrows():
            if j in gt_matched: continue
            
            sim = calculate_similarity(row['item_name'], gt_row['item_name'])
            
            # Boost score if price also matches exactly (helps disambiguate same-name items)
            price_match = False
            try:
                 if abs(float(row['price']) - float(gt_row['price'])) < 0.01:
                     price_match = True
            except:
                pass
            
            # Score = Similarity + Boost
            final_score = sim + (0.5 if price_match else 0.0)
            
            if final_score > best_score:
                best_score = final_score
                best_j = j
        
        # Decide if match
        gt_row_match = None
        is_match = False
        
        if best_j != -1:
             # Re-check logical thresholds
             gt_row_cand = gt.loc[best_j]
             strict_sim = calculate_similarity(row['item_name'], gt_row_cand['item_name'])
             
             # Allow match if Name is good OR Price is exact (weak name match allowed if price exact)
             p_match = False
             try:
                 if abs(float(row['price']) - float(gt_row_cand['price'])) < 0.01:
                     p_match = True
             except:
                 pass

             if strict_sim >= name_thresh or (p_match and strict_sim > 0.3):
                 is_match = True
                 gt_row_match = gt_row_cand
        
        if is_match:
            gt_matched.add(best_j)
            
            # Price Score
            try:
                p1 = float(row['price'])
                p2 = float(gt_row_match['price'])
                price_acc = 1.0 if abs(p1 - p2) < 0.01 else 0.0
            except:
                price_acc = 0.0
                
            matches.append({
                'ext_name': row['item_name'],
                'gt_name': gt_row_match['item_name'],
                'ext_price': row['price'],
                'gt_price': gt_row_match['price'],
                'name_score': calculate_similarity(row['item_name'], gt_row_match['item_name']),
                'price_score': price_acc,
                'match_type': 'TP'
            })
        else:
            matches.append({
                'ext_name': row['item_name'],
                'gt_name': None,
                'ext_price': row['price'],
                'gt_price': None,
                'name_score': 0.0,
                'price_score': 0.0,
                'match_type': 'FP'
            })
    
    # 2. Add False Negatives
    for j, gt_row in gt.iterrows():
        if j not in gt_matched:
            matches.append({
                'ext_name': None,
                'gt_name': gt_row['item_name'],
                'ext_price': None,
                'gt_price': gt_row['price'],
                'name_score': 0.0,
                'price_score': 0.0,
                'match_type': 'FN'
            })
            
    return pd.DataFrame(matches)

# Run Scoring
print("Scoring Rules-Based...")
rules_scores = score_dataset(rules_df, gt_df)

print("Scoring LLM-Based...")
llm_scores = score_dataset(llm_df, gt_df)
````

##### `notebooks/05_benchmark.ipynb` cell 9: markdown; execution count `None`

````markdown
## Step 4: Results Analysis

We aggregate the scores. We also add a **Bag-of-Prices** metric.
````

##### `notebooks/05_benchmark.ipynb` cell 10: code; execution count `19`

````python
def bag_of_prices_accuracy(extracted_df, gt_df):
    """Calculates intersection of price multisets."""
    try:
        p_ext = [round(float(x), 2) for x in extracted_df['price'].dropna()]
        p_gt = [round(float(x), 2) for x in gt_df['price'].dropna()]
        
        c_ext = Counter(p_ext)
        c_gt = Counter(p_gt)
        
        # Intersection counts (min of counts for each value)
        intersection = c_gt & c_ext 
        matches = sum(intersection.values())
        
        return matches / len(p_gt) if len(p_gt) > 0 else 0
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error calculating bag of prices: {e}")
        return 0.0

def print_summary(name, df_scores, extracted_df, gt_df, gt_count):
    if df_scores.empty:
        print(f"[{name}] No data.")
        return
        
    # Filter to True Positives
    tp = df_scores[df_scores['match_type'] == 'TP']
    
    # Accuracy metrics (relative to matches)
    avg_name_acc = tp['name_score'].mean() * 100 if not tp.empty else 0
    avg_price_acc = tp['price_score'].mean() * 100 if not tp.empty else 0
    
    # Independent Price Accuracy (Bag of Prices)
    bag_acc = bag_of_prices_accuracy(extracted_df, gt_df) * 100
    
    # Retrieval Metrics
    extracted_count = len(df_scores[df_scores['ext_name'].notnull()])
    matched_count = len(tp)
    
    precision = matched_count / extracted_count if extracted_count > 0 else 0
    recall = matched_count / gt_count if gt_count > 0 else 0
    f1 = 2 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall) if (precision + recall) > 0 else 0
    
    print(f"--- {name} Results ---")
    print(f"Retrieval (Recall):  {recall:.1%} ({matched_count}/{gt_count} matched)")
    print(f"F1 Score:            {f1:.3f}")
    print(f"Name Accuracy (Sim): {avg_name_acc:.1f}%")
    print(f"Aligned Price Acc:   {avg_price_acc:.1f}%")
    print(f"Bag-of-Prices Acc:   {bag_acc:.1f}% (Independent of Name)")
    print("-----------------------\n")

gt_count = len(gt_df)
print_summary("Rules-Based", rules_scores, rules_df, gt_df, gt_count)
print_summary("LLM-Based", llm_scores, llm_df, gt_df, gt_count)
````

````markdown
## 📊 Final Analysis

**Performance Summary**
- **LLM Superiority**: The LLM significantly outperformed Rules on **Price Integrity** (Bag-of-Prices: 73% vs 46%). This confirms the hypothesis that LLMs handle structural noise better (e.g., distinguishing unit prices vs line totals vs quantities).
- **Recall Bottleneck**: Both methods hovered around 65-69% recall. This suggests the bottleneck is likely **upstream OCR quality**, rather than the extraction logic itself. Text that isn't OCR'd cannot be extracted.
- **Name Quality**: The LLM produced perfect names (100% sim), cleaning up the "garbage" text (like `PET TOY 004...`) that plagued the Rules-based approach.

**Conclusion**: Use **LLM** for final extraction. The cost/latency is justified by the +27% improvement in capturing correct prices.
````
